name: skaiwater
label: Capitol
lede: A Nottingham kid with a GarageBand habit turned a Jersey club loop into a TikTok hit, moved to Los Angeles, and made the album The FADER put at No. 1 for 2024.

eras.title: GarageBand in Nottingham
eras.text: Tyler Brooks grows up in Nottingham on garage, R&B and a father's record collection, then starts posting music online while still a teenager.

years.src: Wikipedia: Skaiwater · Ticketmaster UK · The FADER: cover story
years.h: Tyler Brooks is born in Nottingham
years.p: Wikipedia gives a British-Jamaican mother and a Sierra Leonean father; the FADER adds that the house ran on R&B, pop and UK garage.
years.xp:
In a Ticketmaster UK interview, skaiwater describes a father who was "pro-Black" and played music from Jamaica, Africa and America around the house.

The same father put production software in front of the kid early. The FADER dates the start of making music to age 10, on GarageBand.

years.h: "No Love" with a then-unknown [[Lil Nas X|0b30341b-b59d-4979-8130-b66c0e475321]]
years.p: AllMusic says skaiwater put out "No Love" with Lil Nas X in 2018, shortly before "Old Town Road" turned him into the biggest name in the country.
years.xp: The FADER says skaiwater began posting music online around 2018. Lil Nas X would later take skaiwater on tour as an opener and, in the FADER's telling, serve as a guide on gender nonconformity in hip-hop.

years.src: The FADER: cover story · Ticketmaster UK
years.h: A&R Sean Mula signs on at Cinematic Music Group
years.p: Mula, who later ran GoodTalk, met skaiwater at the end of 2019 and stayed attached through the Geffen and Capitol years.
years.xp: Ticketmaster UK's interview puts skaiwater's first gig at Rough Trade Nottingham, and says the recording method came from watching drill rappers in New York around 2019.

eras.title: A Jersey club loop goes viral
eras.text: A mixtape with Lil Keed, a TikTok hit and an Uzi remix turn a bedroom producer into a major-label signing.

years.h: Happy Hour mixtape, with a guest verse from Lil Keed
years.p: The first full project arrives in May 2021, before anyone outside Nottingham is paying attention.

years.src: Complex · NME · AllMusic · The FADER: cover story
years.p: The Jersey club track peaks inside TikTok's U.S. Top 10 and reaches No. 38 on Spotify's Global Viral 50, per Complex.
years.xp:
The FADER dates the breakthrough to 2021; AllMusic puts "#miles" and "eyes" in 2022. Complex counted more than 20 million streams by the time the mixtape landed.

The tracks spawned remixes from DJ Sliink, Riovaz and Bandmanrill, per AllMusic. Skaiwater told NME: "I didn't expect that at all!"

years.p: Skaiwater called the first contact with Uzi "surreal for sure" in NME, and the remix became the centerpiece of the next project.

years.src: Complex · NME · The FADER: cover story
years.h: Rave lands on Geffen and Cinematic, 11 tracks
years.p: Complex's rundown includes "A Lie", "Auto", "Chloe", "Boys Don't Cry" and the Uzi remix, released as skaiwater prepared to join Lil Nas X in Europe.
years.xp: The FADER dates the Geffen deal to 2022. Skaiwater supported Lil Nas X on the European leg of the Long Live Montero Tour, which NME says included a night in front of 11,000 people, "a learning curve" in skaiwater's words.

eras.title: Los Angeles, Lil Nas X, and #gigi
eras.text: A move west, a US tour opening for Lil Nas X and a move to Capitol lead to the album that lands on year-end lists from Pitchfork to The FADER.

years.p: Wikipedia lists a second version of the project in March 2023, a few weeks before the move to Los Angeles.
Skaiwater relocates to LA in April 2023, and most of #gigi gets recorded afterward.
years.xp: The FADER's album interview quotes skaiwater on what the record holds: "being away from family, long-distance shit, being away from friends. Or learning about my identity out here."

years.p: The single stitches Lil Nas X onto a 9lives beat; skaiwater says they were in a "Pink Friday, YMCMB phase".

years.src: Album of the Year · The FADER: #gigi interview
years.p: Pitchfork's blurb: Jersey club, Brazilian funk, classic soul and Auto-Tune in a "crispy, kinetic mix".
years.xp:
The title began as Gaia. Skaiwater told the FADER it "shortened down to #gigi once it became more of a personal persona." The melody comes first, then the drums, per the same interview.

Guests include Lil Nas X on "light!", Cortisa Star and CARTERTHEBANDIT, according to Album of the Year.

years.src: Album of the Year · The FADER: cover story
years.p: Pitchfork scored #gigi 7.4 (per Album of the Year) and ranked it No. 12 among its 50 best albums of 2024.
years.xp:
Album of the Year lists the record at No. 1 on The FADER's list, No. 12 on Pitchfork's and No. 27 on Complex's. Its aggregate critic score is 74, from one review.

Sean Mula told the FADER that major labels "really want you to have something that's moving on TikTok, which we didn't have at the moment."

eras.title: Out of the major-label machine
eras.text: After #gigi, the output speeds up, the sound roughens, and the label situation shifts.

years.p: Wikipedia lists #mia in February 2025, then a three-part pinkPrint EP series through June.
The FADER's cover story says skaiwater left the major label and went independent.

years.src: Album of the Year · The FADER: cover story
years.p: Album of the Year lists 18 tracks on GoodTalk; Pitchfork's Mano Sundaresan scored it 5.0.
years.xp: The FADER calls the record "straight-up chaos". Pitchfork's review, as quoted by Album of the Year, says the rapper "comes up way short with a record that lacks fun or curiosity." Users gave it 62.

years.h: The FADER cover story: "skaiwater is post everything"
years.p: The magazine gave skaiwater its May 2026 cover.
